activity.notes: Third and final North American voyage, 1541–1542. Cartier sailed under the French Crown within the Roberval colonial enterprise, established Charlesbourg-Royal near Cap-Rouge in 1541 and abandoned the settlement in 1542. The Activity is kept separate from the earlier voyages and does not model New France as a polity he ruled.

sources.title: Jacques Cartier (1491–1557) — Dictionary of Canadian Biography
sources.citation_text: The Dictionary of Canadian Biography records Cartier's third expedition, his subordinate position under Roberval, the 1541 establishment at Charlesbourg-Royal and the abandonment of the settlement in June 1542.

sources.title: Fort Charlesbourg Royal National Historic Site of Canada — Parks Canada
sources.citation_text: Parks Canada states that Charlesbourg-Royal was founded by Jacques Cartier in 1541 during his third and final voyage and was occupied through the winter of 1541–1542.
